Bringing policymakers, businesses, experts and researchers together to turn Europe’s data policies into more data for AI, growth and competitiveness.

This high-level conference will be hosted by the European Commission. It will contribute to a wider political debate on the future of the EU data Policy.

Main topics on the agenda

During the conference, discussions will focus on:

  • Digital Omnibus: Simplifying the EU data rulebook, reducing administrative burden and supporting innovation
  • Data for industrial AI: Improving access to high-quality data through the Data Act
  • International data flows: Promoting open and trusted data flows and securing fair treatment for EU companies abroad

The agenda will be published here.

Register

You can express your interest in participating. Admission is subject to approval.

The event is going to be live streamed.

Background

European companies and researchers need better access to high-quality data to develop and deploy AI. The Data Union Strategy sets out practical measures to increase data availability and strengthen Europe’s data infrastructure.

The Commission is also working to simplify the EU’s digital rules. Building on the Data Act and other existing legislation, the aim is to reduce unnecessary burdens and make it easier for companies to use and share data.

Internationally, the Commission seeks to facilitate trusted cross-border data flows and address unfair restrictions faced by EU companies in other markets. Together, these efforts aim to support AI development and strengthen Europe’s competitiveness.

EU.original_title: EU KIDS Act to restrict social media platforms’ access to children in the EU
EU.source_name: European Commission -- AI Office / Digital news
EU.raw_description:
EU KIDS Act to restrict social media platforms’ access to children in the EU Anonymous (not verified) Thu, 09/17/2026 - 09:36

The European Commission has adopted the EU KIDS Act to enhance the online safety of children throughout the Union.

The proposal prohibits social media platforms from accessing children under the age of 13 and sets an EU-wide minimum age for minors to open an account of their own at the age of 15, thereby ensuring a gradual approach. The KIDS Act also reverses the burden of proof. Now, service providers will have to show that their services are age-appropriate and safe by design.

Commission President, Ursula von der Leyen, said: “Today, our children are engaging with the most sophisticated technologies ever created. Technology that was never created with their wellbeing in mind. Our KIDS Act is reversing the burden of proof - it is for platforms to show they are safe by design. And we put parents back in the driving seat, giving them the tools to help their children navigate a safer online world.”

Read the full press release and factsheet.

EU.original_title: Proposal for EU KIDS Act - 'EU Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy'
EU.source_name: European Commission -- AI Office / Digital news
EU.raw_description:
Proposal for EU KIDS Act - 'EU Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy' Anonymous (not verified) Thu, 09/17/2026 - 09:21

This proposal seeks to protect minors from risky digital services and AI systems, uphold the digital single market and maintain a coherent regulatory framework and enforcement structure for the protection of minors online.

The proposal recognises the risks that minors face on certain online social networking services and video-sharing platforms and therefore limits autonomous account creation on those specific platforms and systems by children below the age of 15 years. By providing one age across the European Union, it harmonises diverging national rules removing obstacles to the implementation of the Digital Single Market, ensuring legal certainty and a similar level of protection for all children in the European Union.

The proposal and its supporting documents are available on EUR-Lex and will soon be accessible in all official EU languages:
  • Proposal for EU KIDS Act - 'EU Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy'
  • Communication accompanying the KIDS Act - An EU approach to online child safety
  • Staff Working Document (SWD) - Analysis of Impacts accompanying the proposal for EU kids Act

Provide your feedback to the consultation on the EU KIDS ACT until 26 November 2026 (midnight Brussels time).

EU.ko_summary: 유럽연합 집행위원회는 온라인 공간에서 아동 안전을 강화하기 위한 'EU KIDS 법안(EU KIDS Act)' 제안서를 발표했습니다. 이 법안은 위험한 디지털 서비스 및 인공지능(AI) 시스템으로부터 미성년자를 보호하기 위해, 특정 소셜 네트워크 및 동영상 공유 플랫폼에서 15세 미만 아동의 단독 계정 생성을 제한하는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 또한 EU 전역에 통일된 연령 기준을 적용하여 회원국별로 엇갈렸던 규제를 조율하고 단일한 보호 수준을 확립하는 것을 목표로 합니다. 해당 제안서와 영향 분석 보고서는 일반에 공개되었으며, 2026년 11월 26일까지 의견 수렴을 진행합니다.
